_source: M. K. Sons Fine Jewels Limited: DRHP dated 11-May-2026 (SEBI filing 101528; printed page = PDF page - 5), restated financials to 31-Dec-2025, Rs million converted to Rs crore. The RHP is on nsearchives.nseindia.com (not reachable here) and was not posted on SEBI by 26-Oct-2026, so price band (Rs 153-162), lot (91), issue split (fresh 1.36 crore + OFS 0.34 crore shares) and dates come from the NSE issue page (read 26-Oct-2026). Valuation base = 9M FY26 annualised (x4/3) because the promoter's proprietorship was merged in only on 29-Mar-2025.

cites.rpt_p: p. 64 (purchases from the promoter's proprietorship before its merger, a promoter-group hotel, and rent to the promoter)

1.finding: Bonus issues of 2:1 (16-May-2025) and 2:3 (Dec-2025) are reflected: EPS 0.60 / 3.63 / 10.26 FY23-25 and 6.83 for 9M FY26 are on the 4,26,90,760 post-bonus shares.

2.finding: Operating cash flow Rs -4.95 / -23.56 / -9.53 cr FY23-25 against PAT Rs 1.34 / 8.17 / 23.26 cr as inventory rose from Rs 44.81 cr to Rs 205.70 cr; 9M FY26 CFO +Rs 18.01 cr against PAT Rs 29.17 cr. Typical for a jewellery retailer stocking new showrooms; inventory days 122 -> 178 -> 205 (p. 101).

3.finding: Current tax about 27% of PBT each year; income tax paid Rs 12.46 cr over FY23-9M FY26.

4.finding: Until 29-Mar-2025 the promoter ran a parallel proprietorship (M. K. Sons Jewellers), from which the company bought Rs 21.52 cr of goods in FY25; it was then merged in for 40,38,152 shares at Rs 176 (Rs 71.07 cr). Promoter loans (Rs 1.52 cr outstanding Dec-25) and showroom rent to the promoter (Rs 1.23 cr in 9M FY26) continue. Disclosed; the merger removes the overlap.

5.finding: Objects Rs 181.51 cr (showroom inventory Rs 151.51 cr + debt repayment Rs 30.00 cr) over 1.36 crore fresh shares = Rs 133.46 a share before GCP and expenses, below the Rs 153 floor.

8.finding: Five leased showrooms (3 Mumbai, 2 Ahmedabad; 6,513 sq ft); the two Ahmedabad showrooms gave 62.40% of 9M FY26 revenue. Finished jewellery is bought from third-party vendors in Maharashtra and Gujarat without long-term contracts.

9.finding: Contingent liabilities Rs 4.995 cr of income-tax demands (3.4% of Dec-25 net worth); no criminal or regulatory cases.

R1.finding: Paresh Rakesh & Associates LLP; FY23-25 restated from special-purpose Ind AS statements prepared from Indian GAAP books.

R3.finding: Fresh issue about Rs 220 cr at the upper band: monitoring agency mandatory; to be named in the RHP.

R6.finding: Aryaman Financial Services (sole BRLM): track record not compiled in this run.

rationale.g1: Revenue Rs 24.91 / 217.32 / 351.28 cr FY23-25 and Rs 360.82 cr in 9M FY26 (Rs 481.10 cr annualised, the base year here) (p. 227); part of the growth is gold-price inflation and the merged proprietorship (p. 64 of MD&A, p. 189). The issue funds Rs 151.51 cr of inventory for a new Maharashtra showroom and an expanded Ahmedabad showroom in FY27 (p. 91). Neutral 20-25% in the first two years as the showrooms open, then 10-18%; Bear 7-12%; Bull 30%+.
rationale.m: EBITDA (issuer KPI: PBT + finance cost + D&A - other income) 9.11% / 5.92% / 10.98% FY23-25 and 13.36% in 9M FY26 (p. 101), helped by gold-price gains on inventory. Neutral 11% (FY25 level); Bear 8.5%; Bull 13%.
rationale.nwc: Inventory + receivables - payables = 44.8% of annualised 9M FY26 revenue (p. 226); inventory days 205 (p. 101). Neutral 45%.
rationale.roic: ROCE 27.24% (FY25) and 26.84% (9M FY26, not annualised) (p. 101). Terminal ROIC 16% (Neutral) given the inventory intensity.
rationale.capex: Showroom fit-outs are small and funded from accruals (p. 91); base capex Rs 2.85 cr (9M FY26 annualised). Net debt Rs 64.60 cr = borrowings Rs 72.11 cr + leases Rs 6.30 cr - cash Rs 13.81 cr (Dec-25). Fresh issue of 1.36 crore shares = Rs 220.32 cr at Rs 162.
